## InkQuest: Text adventure editor released on Steam 

 07.11.2026 2 minutes read 

The InkQuest: Text Game Engine has been released for Linux on Steam.

InkQuest is an editor for creating text adventures without any programming: rooms are drawn on a map, rules are set via dropdown menus. It costs €13.49, with a launch discount of 19% (€10.92).

Finished games can be exported as a web version (runs offline in the browser) or as a desktop app for Windows, macOS and Linux - with no watermark, royalties or revenue share.

> InkQuest is a program for making text games — the kind you play by reading a description of where you are and deciding what to do next. Think of a book where the reader chooses what happens.
> 
> You build the game like this: you draw a map of rooms, you write what the player sees in each one, and you set the rules by choosing from menus. Then you press one button and you have a finished game you can share with anyone.
> 
> You do not write any code. Not one line.
> 
> Draw the world. ... Fill the rooms with things, people and doors.
> 
> Set the rules. Every rule is one sentence you build from dropdown menus: WHEN the player enters the vault, IF they carry the lamp, THEN show this text.
> 
> Press play. Your game runs in the same window you are editing in, so you can try an idea and see it working seconds later.
> 
> Classic text games ask the player to type (take the lamp, go north). Newer ones show a list of choices to click. InkQuest does both, and it is one setting.
>

# Solo Developer's SpellChain Tops 2,000 Sales in Its First 24 Hours on Steam

Big Wiz Games' solo-made spellcrafting RPG SpellChain launched November 5 and topped 2,000 sales in a day, with two bug-fix patches already live.

 

Sam Ito Staff Writer · Nov 6, 2026 · 3 min read

 

Image: Big Wiz Games.

A one-person studio just had the kind of launch week most indie developers only dream about. SpellChain, a first-person spellcrafting fantasy RPG built and published by Big Wiz Games, released on Steam on November 5 for $8.99, and within 24 hours its solo creator was publicly stunned by the response: more than 2,000 copies sold on day one.

...

SpellChain casts players as an exiled wizard living in a tower above a hostile kingdom, tasked with crashing festivals, sabotaging patrols and generally making the king's life miserable on the way to an eventual confrontation with him. The hook is its chain-based spellcrafting system, which lets players combine effects to build their own attacks rather than pick from a fixed spell list, a structure the store page says draws on Magicka and Fictorum. The game ships with six bosses, 25 scripted level events and, according to Big Wiz Games, thousands of viable spell combinations.

...

The runway to launch was itself a small success story. Three days before release, Big Wiz Games announced that SpellChain had crossed 20,000 Steam wishlists, a strong number for a solo-developed debut with no publisher attached, driven in part by players trying the game's public demo ahead of launch.

When the game actually went live on November 5, the developer's own announcement kept things simple: SpellChain was out for $8.99, with a 10% launch discount running for its first ten days, and an invitation for players to bring feedback straight to the official Discord server. There was no elaborate marketing push behind it, just a solo creator posting directly to the people who had already wishlisted the game.

...

What happened next is the real story. In a patch note posted the morning after launch, Big Wiz Games revealed that SpellChain had topped 2,000 sales in its first 24 hours, a number the developer called "more than I ever expected." For a single-developer release priced under $10 with no major platform backing, that is a strong showing, and it tracks with the wishlist momentum the game had already built heading into launch day.

...

SpellChain is available now on Steam for Windows, with full controller support and Steam Achievements. Players chasing the current launch discount have a limited window before the 10% price cut expires, and the developer has said bug reports and suggestions are welcome at any time through the official Discord.

# We reached $1M ARR with zero funding

Kyle Nolan

7 min read Published Jun 30, 2025 Jun 30, 2025

Bootstrapping a side project into a profitable seven-figure business in four years.

We really did it! We bootstrapped ProjectionLab to $1,000,000 in annual recurring revenue.

And I’m still processing that this is real. 🥹

Back in 2021, I was inspired by the financial independence movement and wanted a better way to plan my own life. I couldn’t find the right tool, so I started building.

...

## How we got here

If this is your first time hearing about ProjectionLab, here’s a quick recap:

| Milestone | Date | What Was Happening |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $150 MRR | May 2021 | First internet dollar! (from a post to HN) |
| $600 MRR | Aug 2021 | First blog post |
| $1K MRR | Dec 2021 | Working nights & weekends after corporate job |
| $4K MRR | Sep 2022 | Shoutout from Mr Money Mustache |
| $5k MRR | Nov 2022 | Whoah, public speaking?! |
| $8.3K MRR | Apr 2023 | Started to believe I could do this |
| $10K MRR | Jun 2023 | The final boss of indie hacking |
| $16.6K MRR | Sep 2023 | Dropped to part-time at my day job |
| $23.3K MRR | Nov 2023 | Quit my day job and went all-in! |
| $41.6K MRR | Jul 2024 | Started growing the team |
| $45.8K MRR | Aug 2024 | Shared story on ChooseFI |
| $83.3k MRR | Jun 2025 | 👋 Here we are! |

...

Want to know what building in public from zero to a million dollars a year really felt like? NOT like serenely progressing up-and-to-the-right…

...

For the first two years, I burned the candle at both ends working solo. 4-6 hours every night after work, entire weekends, holidays, you name it.

404 Day Off Not Found.

That was the only way I could build something this complex in a crowded market as a risk-averse engineer with a day job. And I was fortunate enough to attempt this at a stage in life when I had lots of energy and few family responsibilities.

...

Hitting $1M ARR is just the beginning.

And that only counts recurring revenue. With non-recurring income sources like Lifetime subscriptions and 1-on-1 training sessions, monthly revenue has consistently been 20 to 50 percent higher.

With that momentum, we’re doubling down on what got us here:

- Making a good product that people actually like to use (including us)
- Staying lean, bootstrapped, and aligned with the interests of our customers
- Building thoughtfully and sustainably, not chasing AI hype or growth-at-all-costs

In 2024, one folder of starter code was selling about $126,000 a month for a solo founder living in Bali. On October 20, 2026, its creator posted the newer figure: $2,000.

#### AT A GLANCE

What it is: ShipFast, a paid boilerplate (a ready-made folder of code with login and payments already wired up) for building web apps with Next.js, a popular website framework

Founded: launched September 2023 by French solo founder Marc Lou (Marc Louvion)

Team: 1 person

Audience: indie makers and first-time founders, about 8,433 users listed on its TrustMRR profile (November 2026)

Makes money from: one-time licenses at $199, $249 or $299

Latest known milestone: $1,272,892 in all-time revenue verified through Stripe, with $1,395 in the 30 days to October 31, 2026

...

ShipFast went live on Product Hunt (a daily leaderboard for new tech products) on September 1, 2023, finished second for the day with 941 upvotes and brought in $6,000 in 48 hours. By the end of the month: $40,000.

...

ShipFast sells one thing: a license you pay for once and keep forever. Its MRR (monthly recurring revenue, the money subscriptions bring in each month without a new sale) is zero by design.

...

Marc’s own X account is the engine. At launch he had about 35,000 followers, earned over two years of building in public (posting launches and revenue numbers as they happen, flops included). 

By November 2026 the count sits near 420,000. Every revenue screenshot works as an ad for the code that produced it.

This engine fits ShipFast in particular because buyers of a startup kit want proof that the kit produces startups. 

Marc was the proof, posting income from products built on the same code he sold. In early 2024 he reported 500 to 1,500 visitors a day to the ShipFast site without paying for ads.

Two smaller channels added fuel. Skit-style launch videos got shared widely, and a viral YouTube feature in 2024 pushed monthly sales from roughly $50,000 to $135,000, by Marc’s own account on camera.

...

#### THE SOLO VERSION

A small version today: one person selling a $49 starter kit (code or templates) to people rushing into a tool that person already uses daily, built in public on X from the first day.

...

Month 12: $100 to $1,500 a month for people who kept shipping, and many people earn less.

# Damon Chen: Testimonial.to from $1.99 in Failures to $100K+ MRR

Cisco engineer who quit after a family promise, reused failed-project code, and bootstrapped a video testimonial SaaS via Product Hunt, build-in-public, affiliates…

 Damon Chen ↗ Testimonial.to · Founder 

Oct 31, 2026

Founded

Small (solo until ~$400K ARR, then first hire; later small team)"

Stack

React, Firebase, Tailwind (early public details)

...

Damon Chen spent eight years as a software engineer at Cisco. When COVID hit in 2020 he was working from home with his wife and one-year-old. He took six months of unpaid leave to try building products. The first four side projects (Indielog, Howdy, Influeswer, and Backlogs.co) generated a combined $1.99.

Testimonial.to was the fifth. It solved a problem he knew firsthand: collecting authentic social proof for his own failed products. Video and text testimonials felt more credible than generic one-liners, yet most tools made the process clunky. He reused roughly 80% of the code from earlier work, built an MVP in about a week (or less, depending on the account), added a landing page and Stripe, and launched on Product Hunt in December 2020.

Early sales came from lifetime deals at $199. Public posts and Indie Hackers updates show roughly $3,000 in the first 10 days and around $6,000 in the first two weeks from about 30 deals. That was the first real revenue after months of near-zero. He quickly shifted away from one-time licenses toward subscriptions so the business could compound.

...

By September 2021—nine months after the launch and well inside the one-year window—he publicly reported hitting $100K ARR. The promise had been met. Later self-reported milestones included higher six-figure and seven-figure ARR figures for Testimonial.to itself.

...

Early customers came from the Indie Hackers community, Twitter/X, and the Product Hunt launch. Chen documented the journey publicly: milestones, pricing experiments, feature decisions, and the reality of juggling a young family. He has described build-in-public as a flywheel—shipping features that excite existing users while exposing the product to new ones.

Two structural growth loops mattered more than pure audience size (he has noted starting with under 1,000 Twitter followers). First, the “Wall of Love”: customers embed testimonials on their sites with a Testimonial.to logo. Visitors who like what they see sign up. The logo also created an upgrade incentive to remove it. Second, an affiliate program offering 30% recurring commission (and a first-year discount for the referred customer). Chen has said this channel contributed roughly 10–15% of revenue. He mentioned the program in onboarding emails so new users could opt in.

...

In November 2025 he posted that Testimonial.to was at $109K MRR, describing it as “just a traditional app. No AI, no hype. Not a hockey-stick curve, but $109K MRR still feels good.” Earlier public figures (for example, around $70–83K MRR in 2023–2024) show steady compounding rather than viral spikes. Third-party sites have published higher aggregate portfolio estimates; those are not treated here as primary self-reported numbers for the single product.

He stayed largely solo until around $400K ARR, at which point he made a first hire focused on marketing. The company has remained lean. In late 2026 he publicly noted replacing Intercom on Testimonial with his own product, chat.sh.
